What you see in London

Live arrival times, counting down to your stop. Buses here don't share their positions, so the board shows the minutes without moving buses on the route.

Set it up once

  1. 1

    Choose your stop

    Stops nearby come first. You can also search by name, stop code, street or line, or move the map and search that area.

  2. 2

    Pick up to three lines

    Each line gets its own route on the board, so the one you're waiting for is never lost in a list.

  3. 3

    Watch the buses come in

    The next bus, how many stops it still has to go, and the one after it. Tap any bus on the route to see when it reaches you.

A board for your front door

Wall mode turns a spare iPad, iPhone or Mac into an always-on bus board for the hallway. The next bus runs the screen's full height beside the route map, big enough to read from across the hall. Glance at it with your shoes on, and leave when the bus does.

On every screen in the house

iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Apple TV. Save a stop once and it's on all of them: your stops sync through iCloud, and Apple Watch follows your iPhone.

Questions

Which buses does it cover in London?

Every London bus route, with TfL's live arrival predictions. Powered by TfL Open Data. Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database rights.

Is this an official transit app?

No. My Bus Stop is an independent app. It shows the open data published by TfL Open Data, and isn't made or endorsed by any transit agency or operator.

Is My Bus Stop free?

Yes. It's free on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Apple TV, with no ads, no subscription and no account. On a computer without the app, you can also open it on the web.

Can I use it on a computer?

Yes. Open My Bus Stop on the web in any browser, free and with no sign-up. The app adds wall mode, widgets, Apple Watch and Apple TV.

What's the difference between LIVE and SCHEDULED?

LIVE means the time comes from the bus's real position and the agency's live predictions. SCHEDULED means there's no live data for that bus yet, so the board shows the timetable. If the feed goes quiet, the board marks its numbers as stale and tells you when the last data arrived.
